tagline: Morocco's Atlantic resort and surf coast — Agadir's modern marina to Essaouira's UNESCO medina port, a ~90 nm coastal run that today only road or fishing boats serve.
summary: Morocco's central Atlantic coast pairs Agadir — a planned resort city with a modern marina and the country's leading beach-tourism volume — with Essaouira, the UNESCO-listed walled medina and windsurf capital roughly 90 nm to the north, plus the surf-and-resort belt of Taghazout Bay between them. Today the coast is connected only by road, with sea movement limited to fishing fleets and marina day-boats. Demand is tourism- and resort-led and rising fast, carried by a record national tourism year and major coastal investment ahead of the 2030 World Cup. A clean foiling-electric layer fits the resort-transfer and coastal-corridor pattern: the exposed open-Atlantic Agadir–Essaouira line wants Quanta LR's range and stability, while Pioneer II serves the calmer Agadir-bay and Taghazout transfers. The market also anchors a North-Africa entry point for a demand-platform partner.

use_cases.title: Agadir marina resort transfers
use_cases.body: Quiet, zero-wake foiling transfers from Marina Agadir to the bay's beachfront resorts and the Taghazout belt, turning a congested road shuttle into a smooth few-minute on-water hop.

use_cases.title: Agadir ↔ Essaouira coastal corridor
use_cases.body: A fast, comfortable sea line up the Atlantic coast that collapses a long, winding road drive into a direct crossing between the two marquee destinations, holding a stable ride through Atlantic swell.

use_cases.title: Taghazout Bay surf-resort shuttle
use_cases.body: On-demand foiling links between Agadir and the Taghazout Bay surf resorts, giving guests a premium arrival that bypasses the coastal road.

use_cases.title: Agadir-bay coastal day-charter
use_cases.body: Premium, near-silent foiling day excursions along Agadir Bay and the nearshore coast — a clean alternative to diesel day-boats.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The calmer nearshore legs — Marina Agadir ↔ Taghazout Bay (~9 nm) and Agadir-bay day-charters — sit comfortably inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope, with shore charging at the modern marina basin supporting multiple daily rotations.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The ~90 nm open-Atlantic Agadir ↔ Essaouira corridor runs beyond the all-electric envelope through exposed swell and steady Essaouira wind; Quanta LR's ~2,000 nm hybrid range and stability, with no charging-infrastructure dependency at the far end, make it the right tool for that line.

competitive_landscape: Today: road transfers, fishing fleets, marina day-boats; no clean fast-passenger coastal service.
seasonality: Year-round mild climate; Atlantic swell and Essaouira wind make a stable foiling hull a comfort/safety advantage.
regulatory_note: Agadir and Essaouira are commercial ports under ANP; marina operations under SAPST/marina concessionaires.
